title: Increasing throughput of manual microscopy of cell suspensions using solid medium pads
author: Alexandrov, Dergalev

steps.title: Assemble casting cassette
steps.instruction: Prepare a casting cassette using standard glass slides. Attach double spacers made from the same slides by cutting thin rectangles with a rotary stone‑cutting wheel and gluing them with cyanacrylate glue. Alternatively, cut spacers with a glass cutter and tape them to the slide with narrow adhesive tape. For thicker gels (e.g., electrophoresis), use thicker spacers between glass plates.

steps.title: Pour melted solid medium
steps.instruction: Melt solid medium (typically 2–3 % agar in distilled water). Load the molten agar into a Pasteur pipette equipped with a 200 µL tip (attach the tip after the medium is inside the pipette). Place a piece of paper under the cassette to catch spills, then pour the medium into the space between the two slides of the cassette. Allow the gel to set for approximately 5–10 min.

steps.title: Remove top glass and air‑dry
steps.instruction: After the gel has solidified, carefully slide the top glass off to the side, exposing a smooth gel surface. Air‑dry the solid‑medium pad for a few minutes to prevent mixing of subsequent sample droplets.

steps.title: Spot cell suspensions
steps.instruction: Using a wire loop or a pipette, spot cell suspensions onto the dried pad. Up to 36 spots can be placed under a standard 24 × 24 mm coverslip. Colonies from a dish may also be directly streaked onto the pad. Let the spots dry for 1–3 min.

steps.title: Optional: Prepare gel for inverted microscope
steps.instruction: If using an inverted microscope, cut out the gel section containing the samples with a clean coverslip. Place the cut gel face‑down onto a glass‑bottom dish and cover the backside of the gel with a cover glass.

steps.title: Cover samples with coverslip
steps.instruction: Lower a coverslip onto the spotted pad from one side to minimize air‑bubble formation.

steps.title: Mark sample locations
steps.instruction: Turn the slide over and mark the cell‑suspension spots on the back side with a black marker (circles or dots) to aid objective positioning.

steps.title: Image the array
steps.instruction: Place the slide in the microscope, aim the objective at the first marked spot, and bring it into focus. Keep a record of the positions to sequentially image the entire array.

steps.title: Reuse gel for additional samples
steps.instruction: After imaging, remove the coverslip, spot new samples onto unused areas of the same pad, and cover with a fresh coverslip for further imaging.

steps.title: Store gel pad for later use
steps.instruction: To store a pad in use, cover its surface with coverslips to limit drying and place it in a refrigerator. Pre‑made cassettes with pads trapped between slides can be wrapped in plastic and stored at 4 °C for several days.
